It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the Environmental Control Life Support SCOE (ECLS SCOE) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Environmental Control Life Support SCOE (ECLS SCOE) is part of the support equipment to integrate and test the I-HAB Gateway module.
The Environmental Control Life Support SCOE (ECLS SCOE) function is to simulate ECLSS subsystem TM/TC over TTEthernet and I/O signals
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.
